name: Chick
intro: A chick is a baby chicken. It hatches out of an egg.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A chick is a small baby bird.
It is covered in soft, fluffy down.
A new chick is wet when it hatches.
Its down dries in the warm nest.
In a few weeks, it grows longer feathers.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Many chicks live on farms.
A mother hen keeps her chicks warm.
She keeps them warm most at night.
New chicks can not stay warm by themselves.
People keep chicks in a warm box called a brooder.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Inside the egg, the chick eats the yellow yolk.
After it hatches, the yolk feeds it for about two days.
The hen leads her chicks to food and water.
Chicks need clean water all the time.
Chickens eat seeds and bugs.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A chick grows inside a warm egg.
It takes 21 days for a chick to hatch.
It pecks out with a tiny egg tooth on its beak.
A girl chick grows up to be a hen.
A boy chick grows up to be a rooster.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A chick grows its fluffy down inside the egg.
A hen can hear her chicks peep inside their eggs.
She clucks softly to help them hatch.
A chick rests for a few hours while it hatches.
Chicks in one nest hatch a day or two apart.

vocab.meaning: To break out of an egg.
Small, soft feathers on a baby bird.
The yellow part of an egg. It is food for a growing chick.
A tiny bump on a chick's beak that helps it break the shell.
A warm box where people keep baby chicks.
